item.title: Bills No. 1 offense facing No. 1 ranked defense: what history says about this rare matchup
item.description: We don’t see this type of matchup often in the NFL
item.content:encoded:
The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings will provide the football world a rather unique matchup in Week 9 on Monday Night Football.

It will mark just the seventh time since 2017 that the No. 1 offense in EPA per play will meet the No. 1 defense in EPA allowed per play.

Even if you’re not a big analytics enthusiast, you can be assured that EPA per play is a truer measure of a unit’s quality than yards per game or points per game metrics traditionally used in offensive and defensive rankings.

Here are the previous six contests that pitted No. 1 offense vs. No. 1 defense and their results:

Overall that equates to an even 3-3 record. So recent history suggests there’s no clear advantage for the top-ranked offense or defense.

If we check all the way back to 2001 — which then includes nine additional of these specific games — the team with the No. 1 offense is 10-6 in these matchups. A slight advantage over the past 25 years, but nothing drastic.

The average points scored for the No. 1 offense was 25.6. The average EPA per play for the No. 1 offense entering the game was, naturally, a very high +0.217. The average EPA per play in the game against the No. 1 defense was just +0.059, which for context, would place between the No. 9-ranked Patriots and No. 8-ranked Bears (in offensive EPA per play) right now.

However, seven of those 16 matchups featured the No. 1 offense managing a negative EPA per play against the No. 1 defense.

As expected, this unique matchup has been, for the most part, evenly matched… with a reasonably minor edge to the club with the No. 1 offense.

We are in for a treat in Bills – Vikings on MNF.

item.title: 3 players the Titans should try trading before the deadline
item.description: Identifying three players the Tennessee Titans should try trading before the NFL trade deadline (Nov. 10)
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is officially less than one week away (Nov. 10). The Tennessee Titans are obviously sellers at the deadline following their decision to trade star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for two first-round picks and an additional fourth-round selection.

The Simmons trade poses a question: Who else will GM Mike Borgonzi look to trade before the deadline? We’ve identified three players Borgonzi should try moving for more draft capital.

DE Jermaine Johnson II

Jermaine Johnson has been fairly inconsistent as a pass rusher. The Titans acquired his fifth-year rookie contract option when they traded T’Vondre Sweat to the New York Jets for him. That means Johnson is on an expiring contract. He’s a good NFL player who also sets hard edges as a run defender, but getting a draft pick back for an expiring contract would be a worthwhile move. His familiarity with Robert Saleh’s defense could keep him in Tennessee, but trading him would free up more snaps for Femi Oladejo and Keldric Faulk.

LB Cody Barton

Veteran linebacker Cody Barton has begun losing snaps to Cedric Gray in recent weeks. Most Titans fans are surprised it took this long. Gray and Anthony Hill Jr. are the future tandem for Coach Saleh’s defense. Barton is signed through 2027, which could make trading him a little complicated. He’s not on an expiring contract, but any postseason contending team searching for experienced linebacker help should have interest.

RB Tyjae Spears

Could the Titans receive anything in return for Tyjae Spears? It’s a question Mike Borgonzi should be asking. Tony Pollard has been exceptional in recent weeks and Spears is also on an expiring contract. He’s an athletic dual-threat back who is especially productive on passing downs. Perhaps there’s an offense in the market for another third-down playmaker.

item.title: Ravens lose backup QB to season-ending injury, per reports
item.description: The Ravens didn't just lose Lamar Jackson long-term to injury. They will also be without backup QB Tyler Huntley for the remainder of the season.
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Ravens aren't just dealing with an injury to starting quarterback Lamar Jackson. They have also lost backup quarterback Tyler Huntley long-term.

Huntley suffered a turf toe injury while playing in relief of Jackson against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. The injury occurred when Huntley was being twisted to the ground by Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver and had his right foot plant awkwardly in the ground.

Huntley exited the contest following the play and did not return to action, with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finishing the game for the Ravens.

Huntley was ruled out for the Ravens' Week 9 "Thursday Night Football" game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but it now appears that his absence will extend well beyond that contest.

Here's what to know about Huntley's injury and the state of the Ravens' quarterback room.

Tyler Huntley injury update

Huntley's turf toe injury is expected to be season-ending, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday, Nov. 4.

Huntley is expected to have surgery to repair his turf toe injury, as NFL Media's Ian Rapoport reports. Rapoport also compared the injury to the one Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow dealt with in 2025, when he missed nine games because of the malady.

"He faces a long road ahead," Rapoport wrote in a post to X while discussing Huntley's injury.

Huntley finishes the 2026 season having posted a 1-2 record while making three starts as Jackson dealt with an ankle injury earlier in the season. The 28-year-old completed 69.1% of his passes for 727 yards, four touchdowns and one interception across five total appearances.

Is Lamar Jackson out for the season?

While Huntley is expected to miss the rest of the season, the Ravens have not officially ruled Jackson out the rest of the way.

That said, Ravens coach Jesse Minter did acknowledge Jackson's thumb injury could "potentially" be season-ending. And at the very least, the malady will land the two-time MVP on IR.

"That'll be a surgery deal," Minter said when discussing Jackson's injury during a postgame news conference on Sunday, Nov. 1. "He'll go to IR. That's a tough deal."

Minter was asked again for an update about Jackson's status at a Monday, Nov. 2, media availability. He told reporters the 29-year-old had not yet had surgery and that the team would have more information about his status "maybe sometime this week."

Minter did not share any additional information about Jackson's thumb injury.

"I'm not going to get into the specifics of the injury," Minter told reporters.

Jackson would not be eligible to return from IR until Week 14 at the earliest, so his ability to return may depend both on his recovery and Baltimore's ability to remain competitive in the AFC playoff race.

Who is the Ravens' starting quarterback?

For now, that would be Joe Fagnano. The undrafted rookie will make his first NFL start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on "Thursday Night Football" after completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and an interception in relief of Jackson and Huntley against the Bills.

Fagnano (6-3, 230 pounds) spent the final three seasons of his college career at UConn and completed 68% of his passes for 3,448 yards, 28 touchdowns and one interception during his sixth and final college season.

Ravens QB depth chart

Below is a look at the expected pecking order among the quarterbacks the Ravens will have available on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 9.

  1. Joe Fagnano
  2. Austin Reed (practice squad)
  3. Kedon Slovis

Reed and Slovis each signed with the Ravens ahead of their Week 9 game against the Jaguars. Reed is currently on the practice squad, but he may be the favorite to back up Fagnano after playing for the Ravens during the 2026 NFL preseason.

Reed was an undrafted free agent who signed with the Chicago Bears in 2024. He has never appeared in an NFL regular-season game, but he thrived for the Dallas Renegades during the 2026 UFL season, completing 56.3% of his passes for 1,923 yards, a league-high 21 touchdowns and nine interceptions.

Like Reed, Slovis went undrafted in 2024 after playing collegiately for USC, Pitt and BYU. The Ravens are his fifth NFL organization and he has played sparingly during his career to date, dressing for two games with the Arizona Cardinals in 2025 and completing 1 of 2 passes for negative-2 yards.

The Ravens had to sign Slovis to their 53-man roster because he was on the Green Bay Packers' practice squad. Despite that, the 25-year-old may find himself in the team's third-string role as he looks to get up to speed on Declan Doyle's offense.

Still, Slovis played for Ravens quarterback coach Israel Woolfork in Arizona, so that familiarity could help him get up to speed quickly in Baltimore.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Ravens lose backup QB to season-ending injury, per reports

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk will report to 49ers facility after filing for reinstatement
item.description: The decision comes less than a week before the NFL trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Brandon Aiyuk has turned in his paperwork to file for reinstatement, his new agent Drew Rosenhaus has said.

Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Aiyuk will report to the 49ers’ facility on Friday.

“Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,” Rosenhaus said, per Schefter.

Aiyuk has not featured in an NFL game since suffering a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus in the 49ers’ loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on October 20, 2024.

Aiyuk has remained on the reserve/left squad list this season, having initially been given that designation last December after he stopped showing up at the facility.

The 49ers voided around $27 million in guaranteed money on Aiyuk’s contract in July last year after he failed to attend the required rehab sessions and team check-ins in the offseason.

Aiyuk did not report to the 49ers’ training camp this July, leading to him being placed on the reserve/did not report list before being given the ‘left squad’ designation to start the season.

The 2020 first-round pick was required to apply for reinstatement to the league to be able play again.

Having done that, the 49ers are left with a decision, and a potentially tricky distraction ahead of their Week 9 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders.

It is now up to the 49ers to decide whether to keep Aiyuk, look to find a trade partner for him, or simply release him.

Given the apparent breakdown in the relationship between Aiyuk and head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch, him staying on the team looks extremely unlikely. The 49ers, 6-1 and the current one seed in the NFC, do not need the sideshow of Aiyuk reintegrating with the team, despite the obvious talents that made him a star.

The Washington Commanders have long been considered a likely trade partner. However, given his conduct over the past year, it remains to be seen if any team will be willing to give up any sort of draft capital to take a chance on Aiyuk.

As such, the 49ers may be happy to just cut their losses and move on. Aiyuk was, at one point, the perfect Shanahan receiver and, from a talent perspective, would be ideal for a team dealing with injury issues at that spot.

But, at this moment, with the promising position the 49ers enjoy and the baggage he brings, Aiyuk being anywhere near the team is the last thing they need.

item.title: Eagles News: Moro Ojomo is drawing “real interest” ahead of the NFL trade deadline
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 11/4/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

I just don’t believe the Eagles are seriously interested in paying Moro Ojomo after signing Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis to big-money contract extensions. Unless they move on from Carter or Davis … or plan to do so in the offseason. Seems to me like they’ll trade Ojomo ahead of the deadline. If there isn’t a great offer, they can just keep him and hope he factors in to their compensatory pick formula. Now, what can they get for him? Hard to say for sure. I think some might overstate his value considering he has zero sacks this season and only six in his career. But he’s better than those numbers would indicate. Maybe a third-round pick?

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

NFL Week 9 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips and trade deadline news – ESPN

This could be for edge or interior help, in part because the Jaguars have versatile players such as Travon Walker who can play multiple spots up front. Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo is a person of interest here, though Philly is inclined to keep and potentially extend him. […] Speaking of Philadelphia, my sense is the Eagles could be trading some players but likely won’t engage in a rebuild. As one source pointed out, that’s not in the Eagles’ organizational DNA. We already know they aren’t trading running back Saquon Barkley. Look, let’s not be naive — general manager Howie Roseman will take advantage of good value if it’s there, and supporting players are surely on the radar. But dealing big names would be a mild surprise. Ojomo will be a test of the Eagles’ transitional state. There’s real interest in him (from Jacksonville and others). Whether Philly acts on that interest will tell a lot.

Eagles thoughts: Nick Sirianni’s staff stays put, questions at QB and Moro Ojomo’s trade value – The Athletic

Moro Ojomo is a fascinating player to watch during the next week leading up to the trade deadline. The Eagles don’t like letting talented homegrown defensive linemen out the door — and they’re feeling the pain of seeing Milton Williams and Josh Sweat go elsewhere — but it’s hard to see a scenario where Ojomo returns next season with Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis still on the roster. Sports Illustrated reported last week that the Eagles are telling teams they’re not interested in trading Ojomo and want to keep him, but will they pay three defensive tackles top-of-the-league money (assuming that’s what Ojomo commands on the open market)? They seem to have made their choice when they signed Carter and Davis. “Howie (Roseman) and (Jeffrey) Lurie mean so much to me for giving me this opportunity to play for this team,” Roseman said. “I think I was the 23rd DT picked up? If we could make it work, I love playing for the city; I love working hard for the city. I want to produce results for the city. I hate letting them down and being 2-5 like we are. … I mean, I don’t think any door is shut. I wouldn’t say that. You don’t know what the future holds.” It’s a nice thought. It doesn’t seem realistic. The Eagles would be smart to get compensation for Ojomo now, especially in what could be a seller’s market at defensive tackle. If they can land a third-round pick, it would be better than any potential compensatory pick in 2028. Perhaps they can find a way to get a second-round pick. Ojomo said he doesn’t know what will happen — “I just work here,” he said — but he has the talent to help a contending team down the stretch. It hasn’t shown in his statistics this year. I believe in the player, and he’s also a value-add in the locker room. The Eagles will miss him if he’s gone. It’s the reality of the NFL. “I like the way I started the season a little bit,” Ojomo said. “The last couple games being banged up and all that, I want to get back to kind of playing confident, fast. I think that ‘get off’ is one of the things I do at a really high level. That’s one of the things I want to kind of lock in on these next however many games.”

Eagles-Commanders Film Review: The idea that Jalen Hurts was holding this offense back should be finished by now – BGN

I’m struggling to get particularly angry about this offense anymore. There were times when watching the Eagles lose 27-10 to the Commanders bored me. We keep seeing players asked to do things that don’t suit them. Every week, I sit down hoping to see something different, and every week, it feels like I’m writing about the same problems. The Eagles scored their final points with 4:27 remaining in the first quarter. There was an awful lot of football left to sit through after that. The idea that Jalen Hurts was holding this offense back, and that everything would look dramatically different with a quarterback who preferred playing under center and throwing over the middle, should be finished by now. Tanner McKee hasn’t transformed anything. It’s the same offense, with the same limitations, and very little downfield passing game. That doesn’t mean Hurts was playing perfectly or that McKee has played well. He hasn’t. It means changing the quarterback was never going to solve all of this.

Bowen: As the Eagles lurch further into the throes of disaster, shouldn’t somebody down there get at least a little upset about this?- PHLY Eagles

I would not make a good NFL head coach or coordinator for many reasons. High on that list would be, I can’t imagine being at ground level of a disaster like we currently are experiencing with the Eagles, and not reacting with urgency, frustration, and alarm. The Eagles’ coordinators held their weekly media briefings Tuesday. I’m smart enough to know that the manner they convey to reporters doesn’t necessarily mirror their private reactions. They don’t want their players to think they are panicking. Even so, the matter-of-fact, “we just need to tweak this or that” patter at this point in the season is jarring to the ear. Six losses in a row? The last three by double figures? All to teams that currently have losing records? Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has been known to get acerbic when his players aren’t performing to his standards. Not this season, which is shaping up as the worst by far in Fangio’s three years with the Eagles. Vic seems a bit distant these days, almost sedated. When asked to comment on specific players, he either praises them, as he has done repeatedly when asked about Cooper DeJean’s uncharacteristic struggles, or refers to injuries they are working through.

    2026 NFL offensive line rankings: Lions retain top spot, Colts fall without Quenton Nelson – PFF

    22) EAGLES — Left guard Landon Dickerson had his best game of the season, amassing a 72.8 PFF grade in the Eagles’ loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday night. Having permitted nine pressures from 75 pass-blocking snaps in his previous two starts, he allowed just two on 44 snaps this week. However, the right side of the line was ineffective, with Tyler Steen and Markel Bell combining to give up eight pressures.

    In Roob’s Eagles Stats: A big pile of misery broken up by tiny encouraging blips – NBCSP

    The Eagles have had fewer than 350 yards of offense in all eight games so far this year, with a high of 341 at Tennessee. This is the first time in more than half a century they’ve opened a season with eight games under 350 net yards. Last time it happened was the first 11 games of the 1971 season, when their yardage high was 315 yards in a 37-14 loss to the Bengals in the season opener at Riverfront Stadium. Going back to last year, the Eagles have gone 10 straight games with fewer than 350 yards, their longest streak since an 11-gamer over the last nine games of 1977 and the first games of 1978. This is not good.

    Sean Mannion Press Conference: November 3, 2026 – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

    Hear from Offensive Coordinator Sean Mannion on facing the Giants’ defense, RB Saquon Barkley, the use of TE Grant Calcaterra, RB Elijah Mitchell, rookie TE Eli Stowers, and more.

    NY Giants are betting favorite to win NFC East, and have John Harbaugh to thank – Big Blue View

    Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation is taking the Cowboys to emerge as champs. “The Eagles will not. The Eagles are arguably the worst team in the NFL. It’s hard to see how things are going to get better for them this season. The Giants certainly have a good energy going for them as they currently sit atop the division. But quarterback uncertainty remains. The Cowboys could eventually wake up; they have the NFL’s sixth-easiest remaining schedule. I’ll take Dallas to very narrowly edge the Giants.”

    How Brian Schottenheimer is failing the Cowboys – Blogging The Boys

    The Cowboys are a 3-5 football team, and sadly, it’s fitting for who they are. Each week, they are favored against these bad teams because, on paper, they should be beating them. They have more talent. But none of that matters when the coaching puts them at such a disadvantage. Star players become average, and average players become bad. So far, the evidence strongly suggests that Schottenheimer is not a head coach capable of leading an NFL team to victory, and with each new week, this is becoming more and more obvious.

    Commanders injury update: Three key players placed on injured reserve – Hogs Haven

    The Commanders have placed defensive linemen Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw and running back Jeremy McNichols on injured reserve, the team announced on Tuesday. None of that is good news. Some of it was expected based on reporting on Payne and McNichols. This Kinlaw situation is another kick in the shin.

    Buffalo Bills release C.J. Gardner-Johnson, what’s next in safety room? – Buffalo Rumblings

    After his first three NFL seasons on the Saints, the team that drafted him, since the beginning of the 2022 campaign, Gardner-Johnson has been on the Eagles, Lions, Eagles, Texans, Bears, and Bills, and has yet to stay with any of those teams for consecutive seasons. Beyond his on-field antics, Gardner-Johnson, who’ll turn 29 in December, had seriously problems tackling while in Buffalo. In fact, entering Week 9, his 25.7% missed tackle rate was the highest in the NFL among qualifying safeties.

    Vikings waive G Trevor Keegan – PFT

    Keegan, 26, appeared in seven games for Minnesota this season. He was on the field for 30 special teams snaps and three offensive snaps. The Vikings had claimed Keegan off waivers in September. An Eagles fifth-round pick in 2024, Keegan has also spent time with the Cowboys.

    Saints make a set of important roster moves on Tuesday – Canal Street Chronicles

    The New Orleans Saints made a set of roster moves today, announcing that they have released kicker Daniel Carlson and claimed [former Eagles] running back Audric Estime off waivers. Estime is a much-needed addition to a running game that has been virtually nonexistent this season. Coming off their bye week, the Saints are looking to reinvigorate an offense that has struggled to find consistency, and that has to start with establishing the running game, which currently ranks among the worst in the NFL.

    What activating Marcus Bryant, releasing Kindle Vildor means for the Patriots – Pats Pulpit

    [Former Eagles] CB Kindle Vildor: Released. Based on Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins, Vildor’s release comes as a minor surprise. While his 13 snaps on the day exclusively came on special teams, he was part of the game day roster as the fifth cornerback over rookies Karon Prunty and Channing Canada. In fact, the two youngsters were made healthy scratches. And yet, on Tuesday, it was the veteran — who has so far out-snapped both of them on the season — to be let go. The why has yet to be determined, although it seems that his status might be directly tied to that of cornerback Carlton Davis, who had missed three games due to a neck injury before returning on Sunday. With Davis back in the lineup, roster flexibility seemingly outweighed the need for a seventh player at the position regardless of experience or résumé.

    Browns sign G Austin Blaske, WR Xavier Guillory and T Xavier Truss to the practice squad – Cleveland Browns

    [Former Eagles practice squad member] Xavier Truss (6-7, 320) is in his second NFL season out of Georgia. Originally signed as an undrafted free agent by Denver in 2025, Truss has appeared in seven career games with the Saints. He was also a member of the Browns’ practice squad earlier this season. Truss will wear No. 66.

    Broncos sign 3 players to practice squad – Denver Broncos

    [Former Eagles DB] Ugo Amadi, a veteran player who has appeared in 85 career games, spent time on the Broncos’ practice squad in October. A 2019 fourth-round pick of the Seattle Seahawks, Amadi has recorded 208 tackles, two quarterback hits, 12 tackles for loss, two sacks, two forced fumbles and an interception in his NFL career.

    Raiders make two roster moves Tuesday – Raiders Wire

    Tuesday is the day for roster shuffling. The Raiders made a couple moves, adding DE Anthony Goodlow to the practice squad and releasing [former Eagles] T Darian Kinnard.

    Gardner Minshew, Bucky Irving/Kenneth Gainwell, and Ty’Ron Hopper are the NFC’s Week 8 Secret Superstars – SB Nation

item.title: Browns make seven roster moves after Steelers loss
item.description: Practice squad shakeup for the Cleveland Browns heading into Week 9
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Browns have changed their roster up a bit after losing to the Pittsburgh Steelers 27-6 in the rubber match on the road.

Their practice squad saw activity on Tuesday.

RELATED: BROWNS WAIVE RB AUDRIC ESTIME

The Browns waived/released WR Bub Means, P Wes Pahl, OG Vershon Lee, and OT Andrew Coker from their practice squad. In corresponding moves, they signed WR Xavier Guillory, OG Austin Blaske, and OT Xavier Truss to the practice squad. This leaves one roster spot on the practice squad. Estime will not be filling that spot, as he was claimed by Cleveland’s Week 9 opponent, the New Orleans Saints.

Guillory (6’-2”, 210 pounds) went undrafted in 2025 out of Arizona State, then signed with the Baltimore Ravens and was placed on their practice squad last year and this season until he was waived on October 13. He runs a 4.58 and has never been on a main roster.

Blaske (6’-5”, 310 pounds) played for North Carolina and went undrafted this year. He then signed with the Los Angeles Rams and was a last-day cut, then signed to their practice squad.

Truss (6’-7”, 320 pounds) played for Georgia, where he was part of two National Championship teams and went undrafted in 2025. He spent time with the Denver Broncos, New Orleans Saints, the Browns, and the Philadelphia Eagles. He has spent time on practice squads and played in seven NFL games while with the Saints. The Eagles waived him on October 27. Truss played for Cleveland head coach Todd Monken while with Georgia.
